description: Experimental TF3 multiplayer prototype. Probe v68 / bridge v16: resizable Fluent-inspired launcher, explicit connection progress, built-in guide and protected local friends with one-click invitation reuse. v66: in-launcher GitHub Release updates and offline ZIP import, complete package checksums, background preparation, portable folder backup/rollback and automatic restart. v65: stable shared-speed selection under capacity limits; graph-node endpoint capture for street replacement; persistent DPAPI-protected host invitations; IPv6 router control bound to the selected address with compatible lease renewal. v64: automatic Internet host startup, temporary IPv6 default and simplified connection controls without an IPv4 setup button. v63: one shared capacity controller prevents native per-frame speed retries from overwriting remote speed and pause; measured simulation progress; action-compatible money checkpoints and stale correction guards; opaque build commands retain native validation without invalid preview reads. v62: shared requested speed without local catch-up in ordered sessions, common fresh peer capacity, bounded delayed-command guards and shared-speed pause restoration. v61: source-verified single street terminals, stable line comparisons despite millimeter stop jitter and station-group reorder, and one atomic native-confirmed empty parcel cleanup for street stop replay. v60: automatic bounded client protocol upload to the host over the authenticated Internet connection, fixed diagnostic sources, redacted credentials, resumable offsets and isolated background diagnostics. v59: durable incoming handover before receipts, idempotent pre-execution event delivery with world and callback guards, queue categories and progress/work diagnostics, atomic status snapshots and bounded transfer failure codes. v58: capture and replay native bridge/tunnel enums, paired diagnostics for failed build capture, source-aware construction entrance checks and fair world capture budget. v57: observed native builds are never scheduled for a duplicate local replay; continuous host-priority money correction verified against direct booking evidence; native speed-capacity limits; safe duplicate vehicle-name resolution, connected edge lookup and bounded line/cargo diagnostics. v56: faster confirmed vehicle barriers, native acquisition timestamps and purchase funds/prices, skip unchanged confirmed purchase defaults, preserve next-reachable stop and explicit depot targets, fail-closed GUI handover and paired vehicle errors. v55: zero-based edge objects only, precise stop fractions, retained station end-stub detection, host money alignment despite managed loan differences, fixed industry anchors for subsidies, native world data and bounded cargo indexes, diagnostic purchase receipts and batched timeline confirmations. v54: atomically reset loaded-world runtime, immediately release completed pauses, execute vehicle commands through readiness barriers even while paused or clocks differ, send line/purchase dependencies first, and repair and upgrade automatic loading. v53: integrated connection setup, connection-gated save sharing, clear joining address field and one-shot automatic shared-save loading through the native progress page. v52: authenticated plaintext TCP saves with persistent control channels; stable IPv6 selection and invitation reuse; native missing-subsidy creation and host-priority balance alignment. v50: automatic IPv6 router pinholes, verified Windows rules and reliable first-world readiness. Optional TLS Internet invitations over IPv6 or IPv4 with UPnP/manual router forwarding. The launcher tunnels game UDP and parallel save transfer through one authenticated TCP port; VPN sessions exchange builds, lines, vehicles, loans and live calendar speed. v48 holds both games while either pause menu is open, preserves speed across overlapping menu/action holds and streams savegame data continuously with transfer diagnostics. v47 prevents automatic action pauses from leaking into shared user speed and keeps ordered sessions running despite large time offsets. v46 schedules subsidy acceptance/decline with native upfront rewards, shares company names and labels economy failures. v45 preserves the native next-reachable-stop choice, fixes GUI callback data and reports line path failures. v44 fixes world-entry failure in the main GUI vehicle hooks by replacing unsupported log.info with protected stdout logging. v43 reports failed replays on both PCs, reads non-enumerable world components through alternative indexes and intercepts commands in native vehicle windows via the main GUI extension. v42 replaces industry field modules through native commands before station builds and transfers rail bridge and tunnel resource types. v41 preserves rail junctions and guards replay stages. World differences remain diagnostic; a shared save is reloaded only on explicit resync request. Both PCs need the same package. Real two-PC regression tests are still required.
